questions.question: The Nebular Hypothesis of solar system formation was first proposed by:
Which of the following is/are luminous celestial bodies? 1. Stars 2. Planets 3. Galaxies
Consider the following statements about Venus: 1. It rotates clockwise. 2. Its rotation is slower than its revolution. 3. It is the brightest planet.
Which one of the following planets has the largest number of moons?
Which planet has the longest revolution period?
Arrange the following correctly according to distance from the Sun: Mercury, Uranus, Earth, Neptune
The Kuiper Belt is mainly associated with:
Which of the following statements is correct about the Moon?
Match the following pairs correctly: 1. Callisto – (A) Mars 2. Deimos– (B) Jupiter 3. Titan – (C) Saturn 4. Triton – D) Neptune
Aditya-L1 mission of ISRO is related to:

Consider the following statements about Jupiter: 1. upiter has the longest rotational period (i.e., it takes longer to spin once) among the planets. 2. The Great Red Spot is a persistent anticyclonic storm on Jupiter. 3. Ganymede, one of Jupiter’s moons, is the largest satellite in the Solar System. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about Saturn and its rings/moons: 1. Saturn’s mean density is less than waters, so it would float in a large enough body of water. 2. Saturn’s rings were observed in the 17th century and Huygens (1655) provided a major early description. 3. Cassini discovered a prominent gap in Saturn’s rings in the 17th century (Cassini Division). Which of the above statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about Uranus: 1. Uranus appears greenish because methane in its atmosphere absorbs red light and reflects blue/green wavelengths. 2. Uranus has the warmest surface temperature among the planets. 3. William Herschel is credited with discovering Uranus in 1781. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about Neptune: 1. Neptune’s existence was predicted mathematically (perturbations in Uranus’s orbit) before observational confirmation. 2. Triton is Neptune’s largest moon and has a retrograde orbit. 3. Neptune is the innermost of the ice giant planets. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

Assertion: In 2006 the International Astronomical Union (IAU) reclassified Pluto as a "dwarf planet." Reason: This reclassification occurred because Pluto’s orbit lies within the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. Choose the correct option:

Consider the following statements about Pluto and the Kuiper Belt: 1. Pluto’s orbital period around the Sun is approximately 248 Earth years. 2. Pluto is a member of the Kuiper Belt population. 3. Charon is the largest of Pluto’s satellites. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about luminous and non-luminous bodies: 1. Stars are luminous because they produce light via internal nuclear fusion. 2. Fireflies glow (bioluminescence) because they reflect sunlight using specialized scales. 3. Non-luminous objects like asteroids and comets shine in our sky by reflecting sunlight. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about comets: 1. Comets are composed of rock, dust, ices and gases (a “dirty snowball” composition). 2. Halley’s Comet has an orbital period of roughly 76 years. 3. Comet tails always point toward the Sun when a comet is near perihelion. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about asteroids and meteoroids: 1. All asteroids are located beyond Neptune in the Kuiper Belt. 2. A meteoroid becomes a meteor when it enters Earth’s atmosphere, and a meteorite if it reaches the ground. 3. The main asteroid belt is located between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Assertion: Neptune has the shortest orbital period among the planets. Reason: Neptune is the closest planet to the Sun, so it completes its orbit fastest. Choose the correct option:

Match the following planets with their unique features: Column A (Planet) Column B (Feature) A. Mercury 1. Largest volcano in Solar System B. Venus 2. Hottest planet due to greenhouse effect C. Mars 3. Smallest planet D. Jupiter 4. Great Red Spot Options:
Which of the following statements regarding comets is correct?

Consider the following statements about the Sun (energy and structure): 1. Approximately 99% of the Solar System’s mass is in the Sun. 2. The Sun’s composition is primarily hydrogen and helium with heavier elements in trace amounts. 3. Photons created in the core take a long, diffusive path (thousands to millions of years) to reach the photosphere before streaming to space. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about Jupiter (satellites and rings): 1. Jupiter has no ring system at all. 2. Galileo discovered the four large Galilean satellites (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto). 3. Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
